clue.text: Keeping wicket is cooler in the shade

indicators.note: a thing keeping another holds it within, so the cooler contains the wicket

parts.note: a fan is something that cools you
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricketer keeping wicket finds it cooler standing in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping wicket' reads as the cricket job of wicketkeeper, but it tells you to put W inside FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fawn is a pale greyish-brown colour, and a shade is a particular colour or tint.

clue.text: Chief Statistician not as important as he looks?

definitions.text: Chief Statistician not as important as he looks?

parts.words: Chief Statistician not as important as he looks?
parts.note: a chief statistician is literally the head of the figures, and a nominal leader with no real power is a front man who only looks important

explanation.surface: A sly dig at a top government number-cruncher who has less clout than his title suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the term split in two: the head of figures, i.e. a chief statistician.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader in name only, with no real authority, looks important but is not.

clue.text: Something spun by fine writer

parts.note: wool is spun into yarn
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A story spun by an excellent author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something spun' looks like a yarn or tale, but it is the fibre itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf was an English novelist, a famous example of a writer.

clue.text: Water's swallowed very quietly, having something stuck in the throat

indicators.note: the drink takes the other piece inside it, as if gulping it down

parts.note: Adam's ale is a jocular old name for plain water
PP is pianissimo, the musical marking for very quietly

explanation.surface: Someone gulps water silently, trying to shift something lodged in their throat.
explanation.walkthrough: ADAMS ALE (Adam's ale, water) swallows PP to give ADAMS APPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam's apple is the projecting lump of larynx cartilage at the front of the neck, which looks lodged there.

clue.text: Duke (His Grace) prepared to let go

indicators.note: prepared as in made up or worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A duke, addressed as His Grace, readies himself to dismiss a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' makes ISCHARGE from the letters of HIS GRACE; the Duke supplies the opening D.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a prisoner, employee or patient is to release or dismiss them.

clue.text: Minute table a bit short for detached dwelling place

indicators.note: the word is cut a little, losing its final letter

parts.note: the altar is the communion table in a church

explanation.surface: Estate-agent talk: a tiny table that is slightly too short for a detached house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit short' drops the last R of ALTAR to leave ALTA.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is land cut off by sea where people live, and Malta is a Mediterranean island nation.

clue.text: Man in court damned? That's not right

indicators.note: the word is used without its letter for right

parts.note: accursed means damned or under a curse

explanation.surface: Someone in the dock is condemned, and an onlooker protests at the injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not right' sounds like a protest at the verdict, but it removes R from ACCURSED.
explanation.definitionFit: The defendant in a criminal trial is the person charged, standing in the dock.

clue.text: Maybe Chelsea man writes opening of report after one-all

indicators.note: the letter comes after the score in the answer

parts.note: to pen is to write
one given twice, as the numeral I and as the word ONE, like a one-one score

indicators.note: the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Perhaps a Chelsea fan files a match report beginning with the 1-1 scoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chelsea man' points to football, but a Chelsea Pensioner is a retired soldier living at the Royal Hospital, Chelsea in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea Pensioners are the red-coated veterans of the Royal Hospital, so a resident there is an example.

clue.text: My daughter takes a long time getting up

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: An exasperated parent: my daughter takes forever to get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned exclamations of surprise, as in 'My, how you've grown'.

clue.text: Sort of rubber almost a success in making dye

indicators.note: the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: india rubber is a kind of rubber, used for erasers
to make a go of something is to make it a success

explanation.surface: An industrial note on a type of rubber nearly succeeding as a colouring agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last A from INDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue dye obtained from plants, so it is an example of a dye.

clue.text: Weed set to restrict periods of fighting

indicators.note: the outer word confines the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to gel is to set, as a jelly does
rounds are the timed periods of a boxing bout

explanation.surface: A weed is set to hinder fighting, as if gardening were combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common yellow-flowered plant that gardeners treat as a weed.

clue.text: Major river almost a wiggling line

indicators.note: the name stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: the Congo is a great African river

explanation.surface: A big river nearly forms a meandering line on the map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiggling line' sounds like a river's course, but it is the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A conga is a dance in which people follow in a single swaying, snaking queue.

clue.text: Racy, like part of the armed forces?

definitions.meaning: racy means rakishly flashy or a bit disreputable

definitions.text: like part of the armed forces?
definitions.meaning: playfully read as RAF-ish, resembling the Royal Air Force, a British armed service

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as RAF plus -ISH, 'like the RAF', with a whimsical extra F; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish describes a dashing, slightly disreputable style, close to racy or rakish.

clue.text: Given rating, is prone perhaps to reflect and climb down

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating

indicators.note: a reflection shows the word backwards

parts.note: someone prone lies face down

explanation.surface: A sailor, lying flat, pauses to think before descending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reflect' looks like pondering, but it is the reversal signal; 'is prone perhaps' is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to descend a rock face or wall on a rope, a controlled way down.

clue.text: Sloppy food a sort of potato, it's formally assumed

parts.note: a mess is an unappetising dish of soft food
a jacket potato is one baked in its skin

explanation.surface: A sloppy dish and a baked potato, with the meal presumed to be formal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumed' means put on, as one assumes clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess jacket is a short waist-length jacket that officers put on for formal mess dinners.

clue.text: Grotty cell refashioned into student accommodation

indicators.note: grotty means shabby and run-down, suggesting the letters are mangled into new order

explanation.surface: A shabby room is done up to house students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grotty' looks like a description of the cell, but it rearranges CELL REFASHIONED.
explanation.definitionFit: A university building where students live and sleep is a residential block for them.

clue.text: Not finishing pork pie, having capacity? That's a drag

indicators.note: the word is cut before its last letter

parts.note: rhyming slang: porky pie, or pork pie, means a lie
ability is capacity to do something

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a pork pie half-eaten despite having room for it, which is a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pie' is British rhyming slang for lie; 'Not finishing' cuts it to LI.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag is a hindrance or burden, as a liability is something that holds one back.

clue.text: Boundaries of Croatian town make a hairy problem

parts.note: Split is a port city on Croatia's Adriatic coast
the ends of something are its limits

explanation.surface: The borders of a Croatian town cause a tricky dilemma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hairy problem' reads as a tough one, but is literally about hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Frayed tips of hair strands are a common grooming complaint, literally a problem with hair.

clue.text: Novel experience for the Venus de Milo?

definitions.text: Novel experience for the Venus de Milo?

parts.words: Novel experience for the Venus de Milo?
parts.note: a Hemingway novel title, read literally as saying goodbye to one's arms, as the armless statue did

explanation.surface: A wry question about what new thing the famous armless statue went through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new', but it signals a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's First World War novel title, taken literally, fits the statue that lost both arms.

clue.text: Ready with foil, almost completed wrapping cloth up

indicators.note: the outer word goes round the other one
the word stops one letter short

parts.note: ended means completed

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A fencer, nearly finished, wraps up the cloth while holding the foil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foil' here is the fencing sword, not kitchen wrap; the answer is French, used in English fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: The fencer's call warning an opponent to take guard, signalling being poised to fight with a foil.

clue.text: Engage unknown to support officer on vessel

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so the officer comes first
in a down entry, a supporting piece sits underneath, so the unknown goes last

parts.note: OC is officer commanding
a cup is a drinking vessel
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An unknown person is asked to back up an officer aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry 'to support' places Y beneath, and 'on' places OC above CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage or busy someone is to keep their attention or time taken up.

clue.text: Injured, complained there's no hospital

indicators.note: the word is written lacking the named letter

parts.note: to whinge is to complain
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A wounded patient grumbles that there is no hospital nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Winged means wounded by a shot to the arm or wing, slightly hurt.

clue.text: Exhume soldier buried in Yorkshire, say — there's a turnround

indicators.note: a turnround reverses direction, so the whole piece is read backwards
one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a Yorkshire pudding, a British batter side dish, is an example of a pud
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier buried in Yorkshire is dug up in a dramatic reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yorkshire, say' looks like the county, but is a Yorkshire pudding, a British batter side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume a body is to remove it from the ground where it was interred.

clue.text: Piece offered to carrier to pick up

indicators.note: picking up a broadcast means hearing it, so this is how the phrase is heard

parts.note: a carter is a carrier of goods, so this phrase is 'to carter'

explanation.surface: A parcel is handed to a delivery man to collect.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'to carter' is heard as the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard composition, so it is a musical piece.

clue.text: Fast old man breaking serve

indicators.note: the outer word is broken open to admit the other

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis
pa, like 'old man', is a word for father

explanation.surface: A veteran tennis player breaks his opponent's serve with a fast shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking serve' reads as tennis, but PA is inserted into ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace means quickly, at speed, as in 'work proceeds apace'.

clue.text: Graze here -— it's twice the value of a green

definitions.meaning: to nick or scratch the skin lightly

definitions.text: it's twice the value of a green
definitions.meaning: in snooker the ... ball scores six points and the green three

explanation.surface: A field where cattle graze is worth double a village green.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, a cue game popular in Britain, each coloured ball has a points value.
explanation.definitionFit: A light wound such as a graze can be called a pink, from the verb meaning to pierce slightly.

clue.text: Here on foreign trip, monarch is much less friendly

parts.note: ici is French for here, the word a traveller in France would use
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A visiting king or queen abroad turns markedly cooler.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy behaviour is cold and hostile, so a comparative of it means colder in manner.

clue.text: Kafka's Josef joins company scheme: this is one way to get on board

definitions.text: one way to get on board

parts.note: a gang is a group or company of people
a plan is a scheme
Josef K is the hero of Kafka's novel The Trial

explanation.surface: Kafka's character signs up to a corporate scheme as a way of getting aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on board' sounds like joining a project, but means boarding a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangplank is a movable board that people walk along to board a ship from the quay.

clue.text: Pesky rash initially broke out in Asian invasion route

indicators.note: broke out suggests letters bursting free into a new order
just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An annoying rash first erupted along a historic military road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles PESKY RASH plus B, the first letter of 'broke'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain pass between Afghanistan and Pakistan has been a path for invading armies into India.

clue.text: Run for trophy and fall hard

definitions.meaning: to ... along is to run fast
a ..., an animal skin, can be a hunter's trophy
rain ... down when it falls heavily

explanation.surface: Racing for a cup and taking a heavy tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word covers rushing, a hide kept as a prize, and heavy rain beating down.
